title: Reword the README install section for clarity
task: The Install section of README.md leads with a long shell block and buries the one-line summary. Rewrite the prose above that block so a first-time reader sees both installation paths (the agent-driven setup.mjs flow and the manual npm install inside model-gateway) before any command appears. Keep every command exactly as written and leave the other sections untouched.
acceptance: README.md's Install section states both installation paths in prose before the first command block, and every command line is byte-identical to before.

title: Document the run_plan tool in docs/usage.md
task: docs/usage.md shows delegate, review, panel and supervise examples but never shows run_plan. Add a run_plan section explaining the dependency-graph model, with one example that lists two tasks carrying model, capabilities, depends_on and verify, and a sentence on what lands in the ledger journal. Match the surrounding heading depth and code-fence style.
acceptance: docs/usage.md contains a run_plan section whose example has at least two tasks and a depends_on edge plus a verify command.

title: Add JSDoc to the router.ts exports
task: model-gateway/src/router.ts exports parseSpec, resolveCandidates, aliasParams and routeChat with only terse leading comments. Add a JSDoc block to each that lists the accepted model-spec forms and says what the ordered Candidate list means, quoting the file header's existing wording rather than inventing new semantics. Comments only: change no code.
acceptance: Each of parseSpec, resolveCandidates, aliasParams and routeChat has a JSDoc block, and npx tsc --noEmit still reports no errors.

title: Fix the stale version note in CHANGELOG.md
task: CHANGELOG.md's newest entry does not match the version declared in model-gateway/package.json. Read both files, then correct the newest heading and any version mention inside that entry to the version package.json actually declares. Do not add an entry and do not renumber anything else.
acceptance: The newest CHANGELOG.md heading version equals the version field of model-gateway/package.json.

title: Cross-link the docs set around the operating model
task: docs/architecture.md, docs/usage.md, docs/operations.md, docs/testing.md, docs/harness.md and docs/install.md cover overlapping parts of one workflow but rarely link to each other. Add a short See also line at the end of each page pointing at the two most relevant siblings, using relative links that resolve from inside docs/. Do not restructure any page's existing content.
acceptance: All six pages end with a See also line, and a link checker finds every referenced docs/ file present.

title: Explain the aliases block in config.example.json
task: config.example.json carries a top-level $comment but leaves the aliases section bare. Extend that comment so a reader learns fast, strong, reviewer, local and thinker are fallback chains rather than model names, and note that each chain is tried in order. The file must stay valid JSON and still load through loadConfig.
acceptance: config.example.json parses as JSON and its comments describe the five core aliases as ordered fallback chains.

title: Document the .env deny-list and secret staging rules
task: SECURITY.md and docs/operations.md never explain that policy deny rules and the worker secret-staging guard block .env, *.pem and infra/prod/**. Read policy.ts's denyPatterns and globToRegex plus workspace.ts's write path, then document the default patterns, how a project narrows them through .model-gateway.json, and what a worker sees when a path is denied. Use no realistic credential values anywhere.
acceptance: SECURITY.md describes the default deny patterns and the staging guard, cites policy.ts and workspace.ts, and contains no credential-shaped string.

title: Comment how redactKey masks provider credentials
task: model-gateway/src/config.ts defines redactKey and model-gateway/src/logger.ts defines redact, but neither says which fields are masked or why log output must never carry a key. Add comments at both helpers plus a note on expandEnvRef's ${VAR} expansion in config.ts. Comments and doc text only, with no logic change and no realistic key in the comments.
acceptance: redactKey, redact and expandEnvRef each carry a comment stating their masking or expansion behaviour, and the diff adds nothing that looks like an API key.

title: Refresh the lane table in the gateway skill
task: agent-config/claude/skills/break-free-model-gateway/SKILL.md tells the lead when to delegate and which alias to use. Reread its delegation section against the aliases defined in model-gateway/src/config.ts and fix any alias or lane name that no longer exists there. Prose edit only; the YAML frontmatter must stay byte-identical.
acceptance: Every alias named in the SKILL.md body exists in config.ts's DEFAULT_ALIASES and the frontmatter is unchanged.

title: Retitle the mock-provider section in docs/testing.md
task: docs/testing.md documents the keyless unit suite, but its mock-provider heading does not name the file that implements it. Rename the heading so it names model-gateway/test/mock-provider.mjs, then fix any in-page anchor link that pointed at the old heading. Change nothing else on the page.
acceptance: The mock-provider heading names test/mock-provider.mjs and every in-page link to that heading still resolves.

title: Explain glob matching in policy.ts comments
task: model-gateway/src/policy.ts's globToRegex silently treats **/ as optional and anchors slash-free patterns at any depth, which config.example.json's policy rules depend on. Add comments above globToRegex and inside denyPatterns giving the translation table and the (^|/) anchoring rule, then repeat the note as a $comment in config.example.json. Do not alter the regex logic.
acceptance: globToRegex and denyPatterns document the **/ , ** , * and ? translations, config.example.json still parses, and no regex logic changed.

title: Document setup.mjs --doctor and --stats in docs/install.md
task: setup.mjs implements --doctor, --update, --stats and --clean, but docs/install.md only mentions installing and uninstalling. Add a short mode table mapping each flag to what it does and when to run it, taken from setup.mjs's own mode selection block. Document no flag that setup.mjs does not implement.
acceptance: docs/install.md lists exactly the flag modes setup.mjs recognises, each with a one-line purpose.

title: Add a --version flag to the gateway CLI
task: model-gateway/src/index.ts's main() handles --selftest and nothing else, so the version cannot be printed without speaking MCP. Add a --version branch that reads the version from package.json and prints it, exiting before any server wiring, and add an end-to-end assertion for it in model-gateway/test/gateway.test.mjs. The stdio path must stay byte-identical when the flag is absent.
acceptance: node dist/index.js --version prints the package.json version and exits 0 without starting the server.

title: Add a classifyStatus test for 429 and 401
task: model-gateway/test/gateway.test.mjs exercises fallback through the mock provider but never asserts client.ts's classifyStatus directly. Add one test that imports the built classifyStatus and asserts 429 maps to rate_limit and 401 to auth, matching FALLBACK_REASONS in config.ts. Add nothing else and leave the existing tests alone.
acceptance: The new test fails if classifyStatus stops mapping 429 to rate_limit or 401 to auth, and the suite still passes.

title: Rename the private slugTag helper in orchestrate.ts
task: model-gateway/src/orchestrate.ts defines a module-private helper called slugTag that duplicates ledger.ts's slugify in intent. Rename it to slugifyTag at its definition and at every call site in the same file so the name says what it returns. Keep it unexported and change no behaviour.
acceptance: slugTag no longer appears in orchestrate.ts, slugifyTag is used at every former call site, and npx tsc --noEmit is clean.

title: Fix question-mark handling in policy globToRegex
task: policy.ts's globToRegex escapes regex metacharacters before translating wildcards, so a ? in a match pattern becomes a regex dot and a deny rule can never target a path segment containing a literal question mark. Fix the translation so ? matches exactly one non-slash character and a literal ? is expressible, and add a suite case proving it. Add no config options.
acceptance: A deny rule whose pattern contains ? matches exactly one character rather than any character, proven by a test.

title: Add a typecheck npm script
task: model-gateway/package.json has build (tsc) and test (build then node --test) but no way to type-check without emitting. Add a typecheck script running tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit and mention it in docs/testing.md beside the existing commands. Leave the build and test scripts untouched.
acceptance: npm run typecheck exits 0 on a clean tree and docs/testing.md shows the new command.

title: Assert logger redaction of API keys
task: logger.ts exports redact and summarizeArgs and config.ts exports redactKey, but no test proves a key cannot reach the log. Add a test to model-gateway/test/gateway.test.mjs that runs the built redact over a nested object holding an apiKey-shaped value and asserts the secret substring is absent from the serialized result. Do not add a new test file.
acceptance: The new assertion fails if redact stops masking apiKey fields and passes against the current build.

title: Print the registered tool count in --selftest
task: index.ts's --selftest path prints one row per provider through providerReport and says nothing about the MCP surface. Add a final line reporting how many tools were registered with server.registerTool, and keep the exit code driven only by the existing provider-usability rule. Normal stdio mode must be unaffected.
acceptance: node dist/index.js --selftest prints a tool-count line, and its exit code still depends only on provider usability.

title: Cover retryOn for a non-transient failure
task: config.ts declares FALLBACK_REASONS and config.example.json sets fallback.retryOn, but the suite only covers the transient set. Add a regression test to model-gateway/test/gateway.test.mjs that configures retryOn without auth and asserts a 401 candidate is abandoned rather than retried, then add the behaviour to docs/testing.md's coverage list.
acceptance: The new test fails when a non-transient reason is retried anyway, and docs/testing.md's coverage list mentions retryOn enforcement.

title: Add a second MCP server entry to the Claude example
task: agent-config/claude/mcp.json.example registers only the gateway server. Add one further stdio server entry with command, args and an environment placeholder, marked in the name or description as an example the gateway will bridge to workers. The file must stay valid JSON and hold no live token.
acceptance: agent-config/claude/mcp.json.example parses as JSON with two server entries, and no value resembles a live credential.

title: Handle empty quoted args in splitArgv
task: runcmd.ts's splitArgv tokenizer drops empty quoted arguments, so a verify command containing empty quotes silently loses an argument before execFile runs. Fix the tokenizer to preserve empty quoted strings while still rejecting shell metacharacters. Leave isAllowedCommand's allow-list logic unchanged.
acceptance: splitArgv keeps an empty quoted argument as its own token, metacharacter rejection still holds, and the suite passes.

title: Group CAPABILITIES by capability kind
task: workspace.ts declares the Capability union and the CAPABILITIES array in the same order, but that order interleaves read/write with git/github/run/mcp. Reorder both declarations to read, write, run, git, github, mcp and update the CAPABILITIES doc comment to say the order is the order capabilities are listed to a worker. No behaviour change beyond array order.
acceptance: CAPABILITIES and the Capability union share one order, the comment documents it, and the build passes.

title: Cover scout capability downgrade
task: model-gateway/test/scout.test.mjs asserts read-only behaviour for a scout-shaped task. Add one case that requests read, write and run with shape 'scout' through the MCP server and asserts no write or run tool appears, pinning agent.ts's resolveCapabilities forcing. Add a line for it to docs/testing.md's coverage list.
acceptance: The new case fails if scout stops forcing capabilities to read-only, and docs/testing.md lists the behaviour.

title: Add a check script to the videos package
task: videos/package.json exposes timing, studio and render scripts but nothing that fails when the timing data build breaks. Add a check script that runs scripts/build-timing.mjs and exits non-zero on failure, leaving timing, studio and render untouched. Do not modify render.sh.
acceptance: npm run check inside videos/ exits 0 on a good tree and fails when the timing script errors.

title: Name the provider in ProviderError messages
task: client.ts's ProviderError carries status and reason, but chatCompletion's thrown errors never name the provider or model, so a failed fallback chain is hard to read. Include provider.name and req.model in the error message and keep the existing class fields unchanged. Leave classification logic alone.
acceptance: A ProviderError raised for a 500 names the provider and the model, and the suite passes.

title: Record the 3.4.0 ledger changes in CHANGELOG.md
task: CHANGELOG.md's newest entry omits the ledger overlay and worktree-registry work described in docs/architecture.md. Add two bullets to that entry summarising overlay merging and the registry, matching the file's existing bullet style. Invent no features and add no new version heading.
acceptance: The newest CHANGELOG.md entry mentions ledger overlay merging and the worktree registry under the existing heading.

title: Test validatePlan on duplicate task ids
task: orchestrate.ts exports validatePlan to guard run_plan's task graph, but no test covers its rejection paths. Add a test to model-gateway/test/gateway.test.mjs that submits a plan with two tasks sharing one id and asserts the call fails with a validation error instead of running anything. Do not create a new test file.
acceptance: The new test fails if validatePlan accepts duplicate task ids, and the suite passes.

title: Add per-task retries to run_plan
task: orchestrate.ts's RunPlanArgs tasks have no retry control, so a task whose verify fails after a transient provider error is simply failed. Add an optional retries field to PlanTask that re-delegates the task up to that many times after a failure, records every attempt in the ledger journal, and expose it in the run_plan input schema in index.ts. Document the field in docs/usage.md and cover both the retry and the give-up path in the suite.
acceptance: A run_plan task with retries set that fails verify once and then passes is reported done with two journal entries, proven by a test in gateway.test.mjs.

title: Add per-task-type route scoring to run_plan
task: docs/roadmap.md item 2 asks for scorecards that feed routing. Introduce a RoutingScorecard type that aggregates verify pass rates and fallback counts per task type from the ledger, expose it through a new MCP tool, and let run_plan consult it when a task omits its model. Wire it through router.ts's candidate selection, ledger.ts's journal reads and config defaults, and keep today's behaviour when the ledger has no history.
acceptance: With an empty ledger run_plan routes exactly as before; after recorded outcomes a task with no model is offered the highest-scoring lane, proven by the suite.

title: Enforce per-provider concurrency limits
task: config.ts caps worker parallelism only globally through workers.maxConcurrency, so a plan can open every worker against one provider. Add an optional per-provider maxConcurrency, honour it in runPlan's scheduler and in agent.ts's worker loop, and document it in config.example.json and docs/architecture.md. Global limits must still hold and a single-provider plan must not deadlock.
acceptance: A plan whose tasks target one provider capped at one runs them serially, while the global bound still applies across mixed providers.

title: Record the verify command in ledger tasks
task: orchestrate.ts hands a task's verify command to runCommand, but the task file created through Ledger never stores it, so a resumed session cannot re-run the gate. Extend the task frontmatter schema and the render and parse paths in ledger.ts with a verify field, write it from run_plan and delegate, and keep task files written before the change readable.
acceptance: A task created with a verify command round-trips through parseFrontmatter and renderFrontmatter, and an older task file still parses.

title: Validate ledger frontmatter with zod on read
task: ledger.ts parses task and note frontmatter with a hand-rolled reader that silently accepts malformed fields, so a bad status or a missing id can corrupt the board. Replace the ad-hoc checks with a zod schema per document type, rewrite existing files into canonical form on load, and surface a clear error naming the file when migration is impossible. Update the orchestrate.ts, index.ts and codemap.ts callers and cover the migration in the suite.
acceptance: Every task fixture written by the old renderer loads and is rewritten canonically, a task with an unknown status is rejected with a message naming the file, and the suite passes.

title: Migrate provider credentials to env references
task: config.ts's resolveProvider accepts a literal apiKey as well as an ${ENV} reference, and saveConfigPatch persists whatever the user wrote. Add a migration on load that rewrites literal keys in the user config into ${VAR} references backed by each provider catalog entry's keyEnv, refuses to save when the referenced variable is missing, and never logs the value. Document the migration in docs/operations.md and SECURITY.md.
acceptance: A config holding a literal apiKey is rewritten to an ${ENV} reference on the next save, no log line contains the key, and a missing variable aborts the save with a clear message.

title: Require a bearer token on the HTTP endpoint
task: serve.ts's startServe exposes the OpenAI-compatible endpoint with no authentication, which is fine on a laptop and not fine once it is bound to a network interface. Add an optional required bearer token read from an env reference in config, answer 401 without it, and keep the endpoint open when the setting is absent so local-only setups keep working. Document the setting in docs/operations.md.
acceptance: With a token configured, a request without the header gets 401 and one with it succeeds; with no token configured behaviour is unchanged, proven by the suite.

title: Enforce the daily cost budget in run_plan
task: orchestrate.ts's checkDayBudget throws BudgetExceeded only on delegate paths and only when budget is enabled, while runPlan sums cost after the fact. Thread a running spend total through runPlan so a plan stops starting new tasks once the configured daily ceiling is reached, records the spend in the ledger, and reports the skipped tasks with a reason. Delegate behaviour must not change.
acceptance: A plan whose accumulated spend crosses the daily ceiling stops scheduling new tasks, journals the spend, and lists the skipped tasks with a reason in its report.

title: Give ProviderError a typed reason taxonomy
task: client.ts's ProviderError carries a free-form reason string that router.ts's TRANSIENT list compares against, so one typo silently disables fallback. Replace the string with the FallbackReason union declared in config.ts, make classifyStatus the only producer of it, and have routeChat switch exhaustively over that union. Update every throw site and every test that reads the reason.
acceptance: ProviderError.reason is typed as FallbackReason, the compiler rejects a throw outside classifyStatus's mapping, and the suite passes.

title: Split orchestrate.ts into feature modules
task: model-gateway/src/orchestrate.ts has grown past 36 KB and now holds delegation, review, panel, supervision and plan execution with no internal boundary. Split it into orchestrate/delegate.ts, review.ts, panel.ts, supervise.ts and plan.ts behind a re-exporting orchestrate.ts, moving shared Ctx helpers into a small context module. Every importer, including index.ts and the test suites, must keep working unchanged and behaviour must be identical.
acceptance: The suite passes without test edits beyond imports, and no module imports orchestrate.ts only for a type it could take from the feature module that owns it.

title: Validate project-scope allowedCommands
task: index.ts's projectRefuses whitelists which config keys may be persisted into .model-gateway.json, but workers.allowedCommands is not reachable at project scope, so a repository cannot declare the commands its workers may run. Add a restricted path for workers.allowedCommands that only narrows the user-level list and never adds a command, refusing anything wider with a message naming the offending entry. Update docs/operations.md.
acceptance: A project config that only narrows allowedCommands is accepted, one that adds an unknown command is refused naming it, and the suite passes.

title: Dedupe fallback candidates by provider/model
task: resolveCandidates concatenates the alias chain with the global chain, so overlapping chains yield the same provider and model twice and routeChat pays for a duplicate attempt before falling through. Rework resolution to dedupe on provider name plus model while preserving the documented preference order, using the existing seen set. Alias semantics and the returned order for non-overlapping chains must not change.
acceptance: A chain that overlaps the global chain yields each provider and model once in the documented order, proven by the suite.

title: Merge ledger overlays without losing edits
task: ledger.ts's merge path and worktrees.ts's shadow overlay copy tasks between the main ledger and a linked worktree, but a task edited on both sides is resolved last-write-wins. Make the merge conflict-aware: when both sides changed the same task, keep the later status and append both log lines instead of overwriting. Cover the concurrent-edit case in the suite.
acceptance: A task edited in both the main ledger and an overlay merges with both log lines retained and the newer status winning, proven by a test.

title: Refuse to stage credential files from workers
task: workspace.ts's git tools and orchestrate.ts's changedSince let a worker stage anything it can write, including a .env or *.pem that a project's deny rules missed. Add a gateway-side staging guard that refuses git add, commit and push when the staged set contains a credential-shaped path, allow relaxing it only through an explicit config flag, and record the refusal in the ledger journal. Extend the existing secret-staging test.
acceptance: A worker committing a staged .env is refused with a message naming the path, the journal records it, and the explicit flag permits it.

title: Validate provider keys before saving them
task: index.ts's configure_provider persists a key without checking it, so a mistyped key is discovered on the first delegation instead of at configuration time. Add a validation step that performs a minimal listRemoteModels probe before saving, reports a clear failure without echoing the key, and skips validation only behind an explicit offline flag. Cover both the failing and the offline path in the suite.
acceptance: Configuring a provider with an invalid key fails without writing the config and prints no key material; a valid key or the offline flag persists it.

title: Migrate ledger task files to stable ids
task: ledger.ts names task files from slugified titles, so renaming a task orphans its file and breaks wikilinks from notes and PLAN.md. Migrate the store to stable id-based filenames, rewrite existing wikilinks and frontmatter references during the migration, and keep old slug lookups resolving for one session so external links survive. Update codemap.ts and the PLAN and HANDOFF generators.
acceptance: After migration every [[wikilink]] still resolves, a renamed task keeps its filename, and the suite passes for both migrated and fresh ledgers.

title: Design a session store: JSON files or SQLite
task: sessions.ts persists worker conversations as JSON files with no index, and docs/roadmap.md proposes semantic search over notes and outcomes. Write a design note comparing keeping JSON files, moving SessionStore to SQLite, and a hybrid, judged on concurrent access from parallel run_plan workers, diffability in git, and migration cost. Recommend one option and name the exact files it would touch; implement nothing.
acceptance: A design note in docs/ compares all three options on concurrency, review-ability and migration cost, and names the chosen option with its affected files.

title: Design evidence-based routing for run_plan
task: docs/roadmap.md item 2 proposes routing from scorecards, and index.ts already documents the lane aliases. Decide what evidence should move a task off its declared model, choosing among verify pass rate, review verdicts, latency and cost, and define the scoring rule precisely enough to implement, including the cold-start rule that stops a new model being starved. Relate the choice to the lane taxonomy rather than the model ids.
acceptance: The design names each signal, its weight rationale, the cold-start rule, and the functions in router.ts, orchestrate.ts, config.ts and ledger.ts that would change.

title: Decide direct MCP access versus the bridge
task: mcpbridge.ts lends the lead's MCP servers to a worker by name and filters destructive tools, while workspace.ts owns the worker tool list. Argue whether workers should keep receiving bridged tools or get first-class MCP access, weighing tool-name collisions, per-call consent, and the blast radius of one destructive tool slipping through. Write the recommendation and the single rule the bridge should enforce.
acceptance: A written recommendation covers collisions, consent and blast radius, and states one enforceable rule for discoverMcpServers and McpBridge.

title: Specify the handoff pack format
task: docs/roadmap.md item 1 calls for a handoff_pack bundling a task, its ledger overlay, a transcript summary and the command that resumes it in another harness. Design the on-disk layout and its JSON manifest, deciding what belongs in the manifest versus the overlay and how harnessctl.ts should consume it. Settle the failure mode where the target harness lacks a capability the task requires.
acceptance: The spec defines a directory layout and manifest schema, names the consuming code in harnessctl.ts, and states behaviour when a capability is missing.

title: Interpret make the gateway faster into a plan
task: The request 'make the gateway faster' arrives with no metric, target or workload attached. Write the interim analysis: which latency sources are plausible from the code, including router.ts's retry sleeps, index.ts's tool dispatch and orchestrate.ts's scheduling, what to measure first, and which question the user must answer to make the goal decidable. Change no code.
acceptance: The analysis names at least three measurable latency sources with the file each lives in, and lists the open questions that block a concrete target.

title: Decide the server-name migration for v4
task: The gateway registers with Claude as break-free-gateway and with Codex as break_free_gateway, while setup.mjs still carries legacy names in its cleanup path. Decide whether to drop the legacy names outright or keep a deprecation shim for one release, weighing existing installs whose harness config still points at the old keys. This is the lead's call: state the decision and every file it implies.
acceptance: A written decision names the chosen option, the release it lands in, and each file whose registration or cleanup logic changes.

title: Choose the default model for new installs
task: config.example.json and setup.mjs's chain suggestion both propose a default, and the choice sets the cost and quality every new user meets first. Decide which alias defaults.model should ship as, weighing the fast and strong lanes against what providers a fresh install is likely to have configured, and state the fallback chain behind it. Record the decision where setup.mjs's prompts read it.
acceptance: A written decision names one default alias and its chain, with the caveat for users who configured no strong provider.

title: Set the priority order of the v4 roadmap
task: docs/roadmap.md lists four candidate workstreams with a sentence each and no ordering rationale. Decide the order for the next release, weighing user-visible value against the migration cost each item implies, and write the rationale into the roadmap beside the list. This is a product call for the lead, not a research task.
acceptance: docs/roadmap.md's items carry an explicit priority order with a one-paragraph rationale for that ordering.

title: Write the user-facing 3.4 release note
task: CHANGELOG.md records 3.4.0 in engineering terms while README.md is what a new user reads first. Decide the release's single headline, write a short user-facing note stating the one workflow it changes, and align the CHANGELOG entry's opening line with it. Voice and emphasis are the lead's call, not the crew's.
acceptance: A release note names one headline capability in user terms, and the CHANGELOG entry's first line matches it.

title: Merge the rival worktree-registry designs
task: Two internal proposals for the worktree registry disagree about whether state lives under .git/break-free/ or in the ledger overlay, and worktrees.ts currently carries both paths. Decide which store becomes canonical, resolve the duplication in WorktreeRegistry and installGuardHook, and state the migration for registries already written the other way. The lead owns this call after reading both proposals.
acceptance: A written decision names the canonical store, lists the duplicate code paths to delete, and gives the migration step for existing registries.

title: Port the test suites onto a shared MCP harness
task: Eight files under model-gateway/test/ each duplicate MCP client setup, mock-provider startup and server spawning, so one protocol change means eight edits. Refactor them onto a single shared helper covering connect, call-tool, mock-provider lifecycle and temp-workspace fixtures, keeping every assertion's meaning identical and the test count unchanged. This is a multi-hour mechanical refactor meant for an autonomous secondary harness.
acceptance: All eight suites import the shared harness, duplicated setup is deleted, and the suite count and assertions are unchanged.

title: Turn on strict ESM across every source module
task: model-gateway/tsconfig.json emits ESM, but module resolution and verbatimModuleSyntax are loose, so type-only imports survive into runtime imports in places. Enable the strict flags, fix every import and export across the source modules to satisfy them, including the inline import() type positions in index.ts, and keep the emitted dist importable by node. Large, mechanical, and independent of any feature work.
acceptance: tsc reports no errors with the strict ESM flags on, node dist/index.js --selftest still runs, and npm test passes.

title: Implement roadmap item 1 end to end
task: docs/roadmap.md item 1 asks for a local event log plus a watch command, harness hooks that register a worktree at session start, and a handoff_pack that bundles task, overlay and resume command. Build all three across fleet.ts, harness.ts, harnessctl.ts and index.ts, with tests, over a long unattended run. This suits a second harness working autonomously, and it must land as working code rather than a scaffold.
acceptance: Events land in the documented log, a harness session start registers its worktree, handoff_pack emits a consumable bundle, and the suite covers each path.

title: Improve the tests
task: The request is 'improve the tests' with no scope, file or symptom attached. Record it as under-specified: the suite spans eight files under model-gateway/test/, and improve could mean coverage, wall-clock runtime or flake removal, each pointing at different files. Ask the user which outcome they want before any work starts.
acceptance: The task is recorded as blocked on clarification, listing the three plausible readings and the files each would touch.

title: Fix the routing thing that is broken
task: The request is 'fix the routing thing that is broken' with no error, provider or alias named. Record it as under-specified and ask for the failing command and the model spec used, since router.ts, config.ts's alias chains and client.ts's classifyStatus all sit on that path. Start no work until a reproduction exists.
acceptance: The task is recorded as blocked pending a reproduction, naming the inputs needed and the files they would implicate.

title: Make the ledger better
task: The request is 'make the ledger better' with no pain point described. Record it as under-specified: ledger.ts serves task tracking, note search, wikilinks and the Obsidian view, so better could mean speed, schema or ergonomics, and each reading changes a different part of the store. Ask which symptom to chase before touching it.
acceptance: The task is recorded as blocked on clarification, listing the ledger capabilities and the question that would make it decidable.
